kis.title: Gradio Production Architecture: Decoupled Logic, Session State Isolation, Multimodal Pipelines, and Hugging Face Deployment

claims.assertion: Gradio applications require strict architectural decoupling between the Python logic layer (stateless, pure functions testable via headless pytest) and the interface layer (Gradio components and event triggers).

Managing user state in Gradio via module-level Python global variables causes catastrophic multi-user session pollution and concurrency race conditions; per-session state must be managed via gr.State passed explicitly into event handlers.
Production AI interfaces must warm-load models and pipeline resources at module initialization rather than inside callback handlers to eliminate multi-second latency spikes and GPU VRAM exhaustion.
High-throughput and streaming Gradio workflows must enable demo.queue() to protect worker concurrency, provide progress telemetry via gr.Progress, and shed excess request load gracefully.
